heading.en: Three ways to run a government business

hook.en: Posts are run by a ministry, LIC was created by its own Act, and many steel and engineering firms are registered companies. All are public enterprises, but each has a different form.

body.en: A departmental undertaking is run as a department of a ministry, like the Railways and Posts. It is financed by annual budget appropriations, its revenue goes to the treasury, it follows government accounting and audit rules, and its employees are government servants. It allows effective parliamentary control and suits national security work, but suffers from red tape, lack of flexibility and political interference.

points.en: Part of a ministry; no separate entity
Annual budget funding; revenue to treasury

title.en: On the board: Forms of public enterprises

narration.en: Public enterprises take three forms. They differ in how much freedom they have from the government.

say.en: Public enterprises take three forms. They differ in how much freedom they have from the government.
A departmental undertaking is part of a ministry; a statutory corporation is made by a special Act; a government company is registered under the Companies Act.
Departments live on the budget; corporations and companies are financially independent.
Only corporations and companies are separate legal entities. A government company needs at least 51 per cent government shares.
Examples: the Railways, LIC, and BHEL.

narration.en: Sort each feature or example into the form of public enterprise.

explanation.en: Departmental undertakings are part of a ministry; statutory corporations are created by a special Act; government companies are registered companies with at least 51% government shareholding.

text.en: Run as a department of a ministry, like India Post
Set up by a special Act of Parliament
Its powers and functions are defined by its own Act
At least 51% of paid-up capital held by government
Its auditors are appointed by the CAG

body.en: A statutory corporation is set up by a special Act of Parliament or a state legislature, which defines its powers and functions; LIC is an example. It is wholly owned by the state, is a separate legal entity, is financially independent and can borrow, and its employees are not government servants. It enjoys operational freedom, but the Act limits its flexibility and political interference can still occur.

points.en: Separate legal entity; can sue and be sued

narration.en: A statutory corporation is set up by a special Act of Parliament or a state legislature, which defines its powers and functions; LIC is an example. It is wholly owned by the state, is a separate legal entity, is financially independent and can borrow, and its employees are not government servants. It enjoys operational freedom, but the Act limits its flexibility and political interference can still occur.
narration.kn: ಶಾಸನಬದ್ಧ ನಿಗಮ ಸಂಸತ್ತಿನ ಅಥವಾ ರಾಜ್ಯ ಶಾಸಕಾಂಗದ ವಿಶೇಷ ಕಾಯ್ದೆಯಿಂದ ಸ್ಥಾಪಿತವಾಗುತ್ತದೆ; ಪ್ರತ್ಯೇಕ ಕಾನೂನು ಅಸ್ತಿತ್ವ ಮತ್ತು ಹಣಕಾಸು ಸ್ವಾಯತ್ತತೆ ಹೊಂದಿದೆ.

body.en: A government company is registered under the Companies Act, 2013, and at least 51% of its paid-up share capital is held by the central and/or state government. It is a separate legal entity, its auditors are appointed by the Comptroller and Auditor General, and it can raise funds from government and private shareholders. It is easy to form and autonomous, but it can evade direct accountability to Parliament.

points.en: Merit: easy to form; limitation: weaker accountability

narration.en: A government company is registered under the Companies Act, 2013, and at least 51% of its paid-up share capital is held by the central and/or state government. It is a separate legal entity, its auditors are appointed by the Comptroller and Auditor General, and it can raise funds from government and private shareholders. It is easy to form and autonomous, but it can evade direct accountability to Parliament.

54% is not less than 51%, so it is a government company.

narration.en: Recap. Departmental undertakings are part of a ministry and funded by the budget. Statutory corporations are created by a special Act and are financially independent. Government companies have at least 51% government shareholding. Only the last two are separate legal entities.
narration.kn: ಪುನರಾವರ್ತನೆ. ಇಲಾಖಾ ಉದ್ಯಮಗಳು ಸಚಿವಾಲಯದ ಭಾಗ; ಬಜೆಟ್‌ನಿಂದ ಹಣಕಾಸು. ಶಾಸನಬದ್ಧ ನಿಗಮಗಳು ವಿಶೇಷ ಕಾಯ್ದೆಯಿಂದ ರಚಿತ; ಹಣಕಾಸು ಸ್ವಾಯತ್ತ. ಸರ್ಕಾರಿ ಕಂಪನಿಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಕನಿಷ್ಠ 51% ಷೇರು ಸರ್ಕಾರದ್ದು. ಕೊನೆಯ ಎರಡು ಮಾತ್ರ ಪ್ರತ್ಯೇಕ ಕಾನೂನು ಅಸ್ತಿತ್ವ ಹೊಂದಿವೆ.
